summary.text: Ben Cauneac is the Family First candidate for Bass at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he has lived around Loch for about five years, runs an IT business serving local firms and households, and has been married for 25 years with four adult daughters. He also helps lead The Christian Warrior Project, a Christian men's movement, and says he is entering politics to defend Christian and family values in public life.

prior_roles.role: Owner of a local IT company

priorities.text: Making the family central to public policy
Restoring Christian values and the Judeo-Christian basis of Australian society
Backing Family First's stands on traditional marriage, religious freedom and protecting unborn life

summary.text: Chris Buckingham is the Labor candidate for Bass at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC's guide he has led three organisations as chief executive: Casey Cardinia Libraries, the Latrobe Valley Authority and the consulting firm The Fair Co. He was Labor's candidate for the federal seat of McMillan in 2016, losing to the Liberal member Russell Broadbent. His Labor page gives only campaign contacts.

summary.text: Chris Jobe is standing for Victorian Socialists in Bass at the 2026 Victorian election. He teaches in a public school, plays music and belongs to the Australian Education Union. He was a Greens candidate in 2014, when he was second on the party's upper-house ticket for South Eastern Metropolitan Region.

prior_roles.role: Member, Socialists in Schools rank-and-file organising group

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says he stood for the Greens in 2014; Wikipedia's results list him second on the Greens ticket for this region, where only the lead candidate was elected.

priorities.text: I will fight to end privatisation
Full public funding for Victoria's state schools
An economy run for people's needs rather than corporate profit

summary.text: Nikole Schellekens is One Nation's candidate for Bass at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says she grew up in Tooradin, runs a beef farm with her husband and consults on mental health; she set up AgMind Australia, an organisation offering mental health support to farmers. Her One Nation candidate page refused automated requests, so we could not read it.

occupation.text: Beef farmer and mental health consultant

previous_candidacies.election: 2024 Victorian local (Bass Coast, Western Port ward)
previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Nikole Schellekens as an independent who was not elected in this ward; no source we read confirms she is the same person.

summary.text: Rochelle Halstead is the Liberal candidate for Bass at the 2026 Victorian election. She has sat on Bass Coast Shire Council for the Western Port ward since 2020 and has been elected mayor twice, and with her husband ran Tides Bar & Grill in Tooradin for 16 years. Earlier she was a Frankston councillor and mayor, and the ABC says she ran for the Liberals in the Frankston district at the 2006 state election.

prior_roles.note: The ABC and her party page say she was twice elected mayor but give no years or say whether she is mayor now.
The ABC places this in the early 2000s; no source gives exact years.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says she stood for the Liberals in Frankston in 2006. Wikipedia's results list the Liberal candidate, who lost to Labor's Alistair Harkness, as Rochelle McArthur; no source we read confirms this is the same person under an earlier name.

previous_candidacies.election: 2020 Victorian local (Bass Coast, Western Port ward)

summary.text: Sophie Thorn is the Greens candidate for Bass at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in youth mental health and, according to the ABC's guide, moved to the Bass Coast in 2019. On her party page she says she is standing because of the shortage of affordable housing and the risk that climate change poses to coastal homes through flooding.

priorities.text: Protecting coastal homes at risk of flooding as the climate changes
